correctness.rationale: For every integer q>=4,r>=2, the single-cycle sharp centered-variance inequality is supplied by the permutation-extreme cycle characterization in Yancey Section 2.3; its extension to any strictly convex permutation-invariant centered quadratic functional is justified by the same decomposition argument. The exact identity J=sum Q_i-(sum S_i)^2/N, strict coordinate convexity on |S_i|<=a_q, and balanced sign construction prove the claimed sharp value. Equality forces each petal to be a signed distance profile. Explicit formulas for a_q,b_q prove a_q^2>=2b_q and the strict even-to-odd decrease; the odd-to-even increase is immediate. Exact-arithmetic finite checker tests independently support but do not replace these steps.

originality.rationale: The evaluated novelty is the q>=4 congruent-cycle one-point-wedge spread formula, complete sign rigidity, and parity-alternating attachment inequalities. A prior clique-bouquet theorem covers the q=3 specialization and is not claimed. Yancey proves a single-cycle structural lemma, not an r-petal centering optimization; Addario-Berry–Janson–McDiarmid address random-graph spread. No available record or primary source was found to imply the full r>=2 cycle-bouquet theorem. Differently named gluing theorems remain a residual priority risk.

value.rationale: Graph spread is a natural sharp variance/Poincare constant relevant to graph-metric concentration and high Cartesian powers. This is a complete all-q>=4, all-r>=2 classification of a standard two-parameter cactus graph family and all its optimizers. The strict alternating sawtooth under attaching a cycle is counterintuitive and mathematically motivated, not a parameter-relabeling or small numerical improvement.
